It is an array where the first element is the key and the remaining elements are parameters that will be substituted for placeholders in the template designated by the key.

The key identifies the string template. For example, `"gui-alert-tooltip.attack"` (for the template `"__1__ objects are being damaged"`; see the file `data/core/locale/en.cfg`).

The template can contain placeholders such as `__1__` or `__2__`. These will be replaced by the respective parameter in the LocalisedString. The parameters themselves can be other localised strings, which will be processed recursively in the same fashion. Localised strings can not be recursed deeper than 20 levels and can not have more than 20 parameters.

There are two special flags for the localised string, indicated by the key being a particular string. First, if the key is the empty string (`""`), then all parameters will be concatenated (after processing, if any are localised strings themselves). Second, if the key is a question mark (`"?"`), then the first valid parameter will be used. A parameter can be invalid if its name doesn't match any string template. If no parameters are valid, the last one is returned. This is useful to implement a fallback for missing locale templates.

Furthermore, when an API function expects a localised string, it will also accept a regular string (i.e. not a table) which will not be translated, as well as a number, boolean or `nil`, which will be converted to their textual representation.",

=== PrototypeBase.localised_description (type="LocalisedString", optional=True) ===

=== PrototypeBase.localised_name (type="LocalisedString", optional=True) ===

=== PrototypeBase.name (type="string", optional=False) ===
Unique textual identification of the prototype. May only contain alphanumeric characters, dashes and underscores. May not exceed a length of 200 characters.

For a list of all names used in vanilla, see [data.raw](https://wiki.factorio.com/Data.raw).

=== TechnologyPrototype.name (type="string", optional=False) ===
If this name ends with `-<number>`, that number is ignored for localization purposes. E.g. if the name is `technology-3`, the game looks for the `technology-name.technology` localization. The technology tree will also show the number on the technology icon.

=== prototype-stage LocalisedString type ===
Localised strings are a way to support translation of in-game text. They offer a language-independent code representation of the text that should be shown to players.

It is an array where the first element is the key and the remaining elements are parameters that will be substituted for placeholders in the template designated by the key.

The key identifies the string template. For example, `"gui-alert-tooltip.attack"` (for the template `"__1__ objects are being damaged"`; see the file `data/core/locale/en.cfg`). In the settings and prototype stages, this key cannot be longer than 200 characters.

The template can contain placeholders such as `__1__` or `__2__`. These will be replaced by the respective parameter in the LocalisedString. The parameters themselves can be other localised strings, which will be processed recursively in the same fashion. Localised strings can not be recursed deeper than 20 levels and can not have more than 20 parameters.

There are two special flags for the localised string, indicated by the key being a particular string. First, if the key is the empty string (`""`), then all parameters will be concatenated (after processing, if any are localised strings themselves). Second, if the key is a question mark (`"?"`), then the first valid parameter will be used. A parameter can be invalid if its name doesn't match any string template. If no parameters are valid, the last one is returned. This is useful to implement a fallback for missing locale templates.

Furthermore, when an API function expects a localised string, it will also accept a regular string (i.e. not a table) which will not be translated. In the settings and prototype stages, this string cannot be longer than 200 characters.

See [Tutorial:Localisation](https://wiki.factorio.com/Tutorial:Localisation) for more information.

Which locale log(), localised_print() and rcon.print() use for their translation is not stated in the docs. The docs also do not discuss sorting translated lists; the standard pattern (request_translations per player, collect on_string_translated results, sort client-locale strings per player) is an implication, not a documented statement. facts.statement: A LocalisedString is an array where the first element is the key (a string template identifier such as "gui-alert-tooltip.attack") and the remaining elements are parameters substituted for placeholders (__1__, __2__, ...) in the template. Parameters may themselves be LocalisedStrings, processed recursively. The type union is: string | number | boolean | LuaObject | nil | array[LocalisedString]. When an API function expects a LocalisedString it also accepts a plain string (which is NOT translated), and a number, boolean or nil (converted to their textual representation).

facts.statement: Localised strings can not be recursed deeper than 20 levels and can not have more than 20 parameters (both limits stated verbatim).

If the key is the empty string (""), then all parameters are concatenated (after processing, if any are localised strings themselves). Example given: game.print({"", {"item-name.iron-plate"}, ": ", 60}).

If the key is a question mark ("?"), the first valid parameter is used; a parameter is invalid if its name doesn't match any string template; if no parameters are valid the LAST one is returned (useful as fallback for missing locale templates). Documented example: {"?", {"", {"entity-description.furnace"}, "\n"}, {"item-description.furnace"}, "optional fallback"}; without the fallback the result would be "Unknown key: 'item-description.furnace'".

In the settings and prototype stages the key cannot be longer than 200 characters, and a plain (untranslated) string passed where a LocalisedString is expected also cannot exceed 200 characters. Same 20-parameter/20-depth limits and ""/"?" flags as runtime.

facts.topic: Plural syntax (NOT in JSON docs; evidenced from local game data)
facts.statement: The plural form in 2.0 locale templates is __plural_for_parameter__N__{pattern1=text1|pattern2=text2|...}__ with the parameter number wrapped in double underscores, e.g. 'years-ago=__1__ __plural_for_parameter__1__{1=year|rest=years}__ ago'. Observed pattern kinds: exact numbers ('1=year'), 'rest' (catch-all), and 'ends in N' including comma-separated alternative lists, e.g. Polish '__plural_for_parameter__2__{1=godzina|ends in 12, ends in 13, ends in 14=godzin|ends in 2, ends in 3, ends in 4=godziny|rest=godzin}__'. The pluralised parameter can differ from the displayed one (e.g. 'tons=__2__ __plural_for_parameter__1__{1=ton|rest=tons}__'). This syntax is NOT documented in runtime-api.json or prototype-api.json.
